land.text: the Phoenician coast from Arwad to Mount Carmel, one satrapy of the Persian Empire

successors.note: After 539 the page has the area divided into four vassal kingdoms (Sidon, Tyre, Arwad and Byblos) under one satrapy, so the Phoenician kings persisted as Achaemenid vassals until Alexander's siege of Tyre in 332; the Achaemenid dossier should carry that as vassal tint. Cliopatria ends this row's homeland shape at -531.

capitals.name: Tyre
capitals.note: A league of city-states (Tyre, Sidon, Byblos, Arwad, Beirut, Tripoli) with no common capital; Tyre stands for the state because the page has it become the dominant city-state from 969 BC under Hiram I. Before 969 the page names no hegemon.

keyframe_review.note: 12,507 km2 (41 cells) on the Lebanese coast from Arwad to the Carmel edge: the page's core is 'from Arwad to Mount Carmel', and the city-states survived the Late Bronze Age collapse (1200–1150). No area on the page, so the infobox cannot be compared.

12,959 km2, the same coast. Tyre becomes the dominant city-state under Hiram I from 969 (to 936); an alliance between Tyre and Israel at the end of the 11th century created a new geopolitical status quo (the page's words, unquoted). No border move.

Fix 2026-10-19 (reviewer decision): the western cells (Tunisia, Sicily, Libya, later Iberia and Morocco) are dropped from this dossier because phoenician-colonies (af-02, founded -900) and carthage (from -814) draw them; the homeland is the Levant part of the shape. Earlier note: 14,934 km2: the homeland (40 cells) plus six western cells (Tunisia, Sicily and the Libyan coast, lon 9.7–14.8 E). The page has Tyre founding colonies from the late 10th century BC in Cyprus, Sardinia, Iberia, the Balearic Islands, Sicily, Malta, Morocco and Tunisia, so the western cells are the first colonies, a Tyrian colonial sphere that the Colonies and Carthage dossiers (af-02) also draw from -900 and -814. Kept (unverified at cell level: page budget).

correction.text: Cliopatria's -900 shape cut to the Levant: the Phoenician coast from Arwad to the Carmel edge, valid -900..-801, without the western colonies

keyframe_review.note: Fix 2026-10-19 (reviewer decision): the western cells (Tunisia, Sicily, Libya, later Iberia and Morocco) are dropped from this dossier because phoenician-colonies (af-02, founded -900) and carthage (from -814) draw them; the homeland is the Levant part of the shape. Earlier note: 25,425 km2: the homeland (36 cells) plus the colonial sphere to Iberia and Morocco (west to 6.2 W, Cyprus on the east); the step is Cliopatria's. Carthage was founded 814 BC (Timaeus's date, which modern historians generally accept).

correction.text: Cliopatria's -800 shape cut to the Levant: the Phoenician coast from Arwad to the Carmel edge, valid -800..-751, without the western colonies
Cliopatria's -750 shape cut to the Levant: the Phoenician coast from Arwad to the Carmel edge, valid -750..-739, without the western colonies

keyframe_review.note: Fix 2026-10-19 (reviewer decision): the western cells (Tunisia, Sicily, Libya, later Iberia and Morocco) are dropped from this dossier because phoenician-colonies (af-02, founded -900) and carthage (from -814) draw them; the homeland is the Levant part of the shape. Earlier note: 28,357 km2 to -676 is too long in the east: in 738 BC most of the Levant, including northern Phoenicia, was annexed by Assyria while Tyre and Byblos remained tributary states. The shape stands for -750..-739 only; -738..-676 follows in two keyframes. The western colonial sphere stays as Cliopatria draws it until it leaves the row in -675.

correction.text: the Phoenician coast without northern Phoenicia (Tripoli to Arwad and Simyra), annexed in 738

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the 750 shape without northern Phoenicia (Tripoli to Arwad and Simyra, 9 cells), annexed by Assyria in 738. The page does not name the lost cities; the North Lebanon and Tartus provinces stand for 'northern Phoenicia'. Fix 2026-10-19: the western cells that the first version added to this shape are dropped (phoenician-colonies and carthage draw them).

New keyframe: Esarhaddon captured the rebellious Sidon in 677 and made it an Assyrian province (the Esarhaddon page); the 25 km circle at Saida is cut out. Fix 2026-10-19: the western cells are dropped here too.

correction.text: Tyre, Byblos and the central coast, the homeland without northern Phoenicia (738) and Sidon (677)

keyframe_review.note: 15,496 km2 of western cells only (Tunisia, Libya, Algeria; lon 7.3–14.9 E): Cliopatria drops the homeland in -675 and keeps a copy of the colonies; its 14,867 km2 -650 shape is within 0.1 percent of the Phoenician Colonies row's 14,878 km2 shape. The homeland did not vanish (Tyre and Byblos were tributaries and Tyre was not destroyed in 585–573) and the colonies are drawn by phoenician-colonies and carthage (af-02). The shape to use is the homeland under Assyria.

14,867 km2, again western cells only (Tunisia, Libya, Morocco), a duplicate of the Phoenician Colonies shape. Same correction: the homeland under Assyria; the western cells belong to phoenician-colonies (-700..-616) and carthage (from -650).

correction.text: the Phoenician coast without northern Phoenicia (738) and Sidon (677), valid -615..-539; no Cyprus, no western cells

keyframe_review.note: Fix 2026-10-19 (reviewer): Cliopatria's 35,130 km2 shape returns the full coast (northern Phoenicia and Sidon again) plus Sardinia, Sicily, Libya and Iberia, and the first version kept the Kition cells of Cyprus. None of that is on the Phoenicia page, which gives no date for any regained independence after Assyria ('Phoenician cities revolted several times throughout the reigns of the first Babylonian kings') and does not mention Cyprus or Kition; the western cells belong to phoenician-colonies and carthage, Kition to a kition dossier (me-04-x), and the neo-assyrian-empire and neo-babylonian-empire dossiers send the west from Assyria to Babylon in -609. The shape is therefore the homeland as it stood after -677, kept to -539.

correction.text: the Carthaginian sphere, drawn under carthage, not phoenicia

keyframe_review.note: 22,314 km2, western cells only (Italy, Libya, Spain): Carthage's sphere, drawn by the carthage dossier (keyframe carthage_-615 to -501). Cyrus took Babylon in 539 and the Levant became one satrapy; the Phoenician homeland is then Achaemenid. No Phoenician state of this shape exists after -539.

region.text: the Phoenician coast from Arwad to the Carmel edge

ledger.note: c. 1150 BC: the Phoenician city-states stand free after the Bronze Age collapse. The page says the Late Bronze Age collapse (1200–1150) severely weakened or destroyed Egypt and the Hittites while the Phoenician cities survived, that Tyre, Sidon and Byblos kept their independence by 1230, and that the core area stretches 'from Arwad to Mount Carmel'. The page gives no boundary.

region.text: northern Phoenicia, Tripoli to Arwad and Simyra

ledger.note: 738 BC: Assyria annexes northern Phoenicia. The page has most of the Levant, including northern Phoenicia, annexed in 738 while Tyre and Byblos remain tributary states The Tiglath-Pileser III page (second page) has him annex Pattin in 738 and create the provinces of Kullania, Hatarikka and Simirra, with Byblos paying tribute and Tyre paying tribute after 740. The cities lost are the researcher's reading: Simirra (Tell Kazel) is the coastal province, so the Tartus and North Lebanon provinces stand for it.

region.text: Tyre, Byblos and the central coast, the homeland without northern Phoenicia

ledger.note: 738 BC: Tyre and Byblos become Assyrian tributaries. 'By 738 BC, most of the Levant, including northern Phoenicia, was annexed' and 'only Tyre and Byblos, the most powerful city-states, remained tributary states outside of direct Assyrian control' (Phoenicia page, reopened 2026-10-19); the Tiglath-Pileser III page has Tyre pay tribute after Arpad and 'capture' it in 732. Phoenicia is the vassal, the Assyrian empire the suzerain. Confidence 2, not the reviewer's 3: the page names Tyre and Byblos only, and the region (the homeland minus the north, Sidon's land included until -677) is my reading; me-02 should mirror it.

677 BC: Esarhaddon captures Sidon. The page has him capturing the rebellious Sidon in 677 (its king Abdi-Milkutti escaped by boat and was executed in 676) and reducing it to an Assyrian province; Baal of Tyre received two cities that had been under Sidon's control (no names). The Phoenicia page says only that Esarhaddon destroyed Sidon, enslaved its inhabitants and built a new city on its ruins, in the 7th century.

region.text: the Phoenician cities that Assyria left as tributaries

ledger.note: 609 BC (bridged): the tribute to Assyria ends with the empire; neo-assyrian-empire /ledger/58 and neo-babylonian-empire /ledger/3 send the west to Babylon that year. The Phoenicia page says Assyria 'experienced a swift and violent fall, destroyed by a Babylonian uprising and an invasion by the Medes' and that the Phoenician cities then revolted against the first Babylonian kings, with no year and no restoration of Sidon or northern Phoenicia.

585 BC: Nebuchadnezzar II besieges Tyre. The Phoenicia page gives the consensus dating of the siege as 585–573 BC and says the city was not destroyed; the Tyre page: 'It came under Babylonian rule in 572 BC.'

573 BC: the siege of Tyre ends. The Tyre page has Tyre under Babylonian rule from 572 BC and the Sidon page has Sidon subjugated by Nebuchadnezzar II as part of the Neo-Babylonian Empire (no date); both are the suzerain's vassal events, not a loss of Phoenician land.

region.text: Tyre and the Phoenician cities under Babylonian rule

ledger.note: 573 BC: Tyre and the Phoenician cities pass under Babylonian rule. The siege of Tyre 'lasted from 585 BC through 573 BC' and Tyre adopted judges 'during the period of Babylonian rule' (Phoenicia page, reopened 2026-10-19); the Tyre page has it 'under Babylonian rule in 572 BC'. Phoenicia is the vassal, Babylon the suzerain; mirrors neo-babylonian-empire /ledger/8.

region.text: the Phoenician coast, one Persian satrapy of four vassal kingdoms

ledger.note: 539 BC: Cyrus the Great takes Babylon and the Levant becomes one satrapy. The page has the Levant consolidated into a single satrapy with a yearly tribute of 350 talents after Cyrus took Babylon in 539, and the Phoenician area divided into four vassal kingdoms (Sidon, Tyre, Arwad and Byblos). [Reviewer me-04-a: confidence 3 to 2; the Phoenicia page dates Cyrus's taking of Babylon to 539 and says the Phoenicians 'yielded themselves to the Persians' without a year for the Phoenician cities.] [Fix 2026-10-19: region reduced to the homeland as held after -738 and -677.]

539 BC: the Phoenician city-states pass under Persian rule. Alexander besieged Tyre for roughly seven months in 332 BC; Roman annexation came in 64 BC (infobox). Cliopatria's homeland shape runs to -531.

region.text: the Phoenician cities under Babylonian rule

ledger.note: 539 BC: Babylonian rule ends when Cyrus takes Babylon. 'In 539 BC, Cyrus the Great ... took Babylon' and the Phoenicians 'yielded themselves to the Persians' (Phoenicia page, no year for the cities); mirrors neo-babylonian-empire /ledger/11.

wars.name: Assyrian annexation of northern Phoenicia (Tiglath-Pileser III)
wars.outcome: Northern Phoenicia annexed; Tyre and Byblos left as tributary states.
wars.note: Shalmaneser III (from 858 BC) had already demanded tribute from the 'kings of the seacoast', likely including Tyre, Sidon, Arwad and Byblos.

wars.name: Tiglath-Pileser III's Levant campaigns and the capture of Tyre
wars.outcome: Pattin and northern Phoenicia annexed in 738 (provinces Kullania, Hatarikka, Simirra), Byblos and Tyre paying tribute; in 732 Damascus fell and the page also records that Tyre was captured, without saying whether it was annexed or left as a vassal.
wars.note: The Phoenicia page has Tyre untouched until Sargon II's siege of 721; the two pages differ on 732.

wars.name: Sargon II's siege of Tyre
wars.outcome: Sargon II besieges Tyre and crushes the rebellion; no territory changes.
wars.note: The page dates it 721 BC and names no result for the siege.

wars.name: Esarhaddon's capture of Sidon
wars.outcome: Sidon taken in 677, its king executed in 676, the city made an Assyrian province; two Sidonian cities given to Baal of Tyre.
wars.note: The Phoenicia page says only that Esarhaddon destroyed Sidon and built a new city on its ruins.

wars.name: Nebuchadnezzar II's siege of Tyre
wars.outcome: A thirteen-year siege; the city was not destroyed and came under Babylonian rule in 572 (Tyre page).
wars.note: The page's range is 585 to 573 BC, the consensus dating.

wars.name: Persian conquest of the Levant
wars.outcome: Cyrus takes Babylon; the Levant is consolidated into a single satrapy and the Phoenician area divided into four vassal kingdoms.
wars.note: The page names no Phoenician resistance.

certainty.note: The city-states' territories were thin coastal strips between the sea and the mountains and no treaty or survey line survives; the western colonies are points, not areas.

sources.title: Phoenicia
sources.note: Core area 'from Arwad to Mount Carmel', independence 1230, Hiram I 969, colonies from the late 10th century, Carthage 814, Assyrian annexation 738, Sargon II 721, Nebuchadnezzar 585–573, Cyrus 539, Alexander 332. No area.

sources.title: Tyre, Lebanon
sources.note: Thin: Alexander 332 and 'It came under Babylonian rule in 572 BC'; no Assyrian or Hiram dates.

sources.title: Sidon
sources.note: Thin: Nebuchadnezzar II subjugated Sidon (no date); Persian period; Alexander 333; no Esarhaddon date.

sources.title: Esarhaddon
sources.note: Sidon captured 677 and made a province, Abdi-Milkutti executed 676, Baal of Tyre receives two cities.

sources.title: Tiglath-Pileser III
sources.note: 738: Pattin annexed and the provinces of Kullania, Hatarikka and Simirra created, Byblos and Tyre paying tribute; 732: Tyre captured (no detail).

notes: CLIOPATRIA ROW: 'Phoenicia' -1150..-501, 9 shapes, an umbrella member of (Phoenician Empire). It is not one state: the homeland city-states of the Lebanese coast (this dossier) plus a western colonial sphere that the Phoenician Colonies and Carthage dossiers (af-02) also draw. The -675 and -650 shapes are western cells only and duplicate Phoenician Colonies (14,867 vs 14,878 km2); the -530 shape is Carthage's sphere. This dossier keeps the homeland only and ends it in -539 (Persian satrapy; Cliopatria ends the homeland shape at -531); the western cells are dropped (fix pass, reviewer decision) because phoenician-colonies and carthage draw them. NEW KEYFRAMES: -738 (northern Phoenicia annexed), -677 (Sidon), and corrections for -675, -650 (homeland under Assyria; Cliopatria has none), -615 (homeland only) and -530 (no Phoenician shape). The cuts are set operations on Cliopatria's own shapes with provincial names standing for the cities, not page boundaries. TIMING GAP: -738..-609 shows the homeland as an Assyrian tributary (vassal_start/vassal_end) while the Neo-Assyrian shape also covers it; the -615 'return' of northern Phoenicia and Sidon is Cliopatria's, is on no page and is NOT drawn (fix pass). Tyre fell under Babylon in 572 (Tyre page) and Sidon was subjugated (Sidon page): recorded here from the fix pass as vassal_start -573 / vassal_end -539. NOT DRAWN: Hiram I's alliance with Solomon (no territory), Cyprus and the three Kition cells (dropped in the fix pass: Kition has its own dossier wanted and twenty-sixth-dynasty-of-egypt's -570 loss should name kition, not phoenicia), Utica, Gadir, Motya (the Phoenicia page does not date them; af-02's pages do). AREA: no infobox area. PAGE BUDGET: five pages (Phoenicia, Tyre, Sidon, Esarhaddon, Tiglath-Pileser III), two of them thin (Tyre, Sidon); the Phoenicia page is the source of nearly everything. A gap-filler should open 'Siege of Tyre (586-573 BC)', 'Byblos' and 'Arwad'. COUNTERPARTS WANTED: kition (Cyprus), canaanite-city-states (the Bronze Age predecessors; none claimed here), neo-babylonian-empire and achaemenid-empire for the vassal tint 585–539. FIX PASS 2026-10-19 (reviewer verdict fail): (1) western colonies dropped: ledger gains -900, -800, -750 and the -675 split deleted; keyframes -900, -800, -750 adjusted to the Levant part; -738 and -677 corrections lose their western union; -675, -650 and -530 'wrong' verdicts stand. The colonies are drawn by phoenician-colonies (af-02, -900..-616) and carthage (from -814). (2) The -615 gain from neo-assyrian-empire deleted (no page; conflicts with the -609 transfer of the west) and the -615 keyframe corrected to the homeland minus the north and Sidon, to -539; the -539 loss and dissolve and the successor land use the same shape. (3) Added vassal_start/vassal_end for neo-assyrian-empire (-738..-609) and neo-babylonian-empire (-573..-539); the Assyrian start is confidence 2 where the reviewer said 3 (the page names Tyre and Byblos, not the region). (4) Kition cells and the -570 loss and keyframe deleted; twenty-sixth-dynasty-of-egypt should route its -570 counterpart to kition (me-04-x). NOT DONE (thin): Hiram I territory, Sidon's later status (Babylonian king, Persian vassal kingdom): the Phoenicia and Tyre pages (reopened) give neither. me-02 should add the mirrors: vassal_start -738 and a gain from phoenicia in -738 and -677 (Esarhaddon page: 677, not -675).
